title: Nightly CI and performance regression harness
objective: Wire the full Phase 10 benchmark registry into nightly CI and activate local performance-regression tests.

plan_assets.asset_description: Phase E9 nightly CI and performance harness scope.

scope: Wire nightly CI to full benchmark settings.
Avoid GPU-only requirements for local tests.
implementation_steps: Run GitNexus impact before editing existing workflow or perf harness symbols.
Add or update the nightly workflow to run full benchmark settings.
Replace performance-regression stubs with local smoke tests.
Assert baseline comparison output and failure thresholds.
Run local smoke perf tests and relevant CI validation commands.
acceptance_criteria: Local performance test uses smoke settings.
Nightly workflow uses full benchmark settings.
No GPU-only requirement exists for local tests.
P10-10 can be closed after this task passes.

cases: nightly workflow includes full benchmark command

risks: CI runtime can become too expensive; mitigate by keeping local smoke tests separate from nightly full settings.
completion_notes: Added .github/workflows/nightly.yml (cron 06:00 UTC + workflow_dispatch). Two jobs on ubuntu-latest (no GPU): nightly-tests runs `pytest -m 'nightly or regression'`; perf-regression runs the new mechdsl.verify.perf.run_compare CLI which loads the baseline, runs the smoke registry, compares at 10% tolerance, writes the ComparisonReport as a workflow artifact, and exits non-zero on >10% regression.
Added mechdsl/verify/perf/run_compare.py — reusable CLI for the same compare logic; runnable locally via `uv run python -m mechdsl.verify.perf.run_compare`.

Activated all three existing PLAN-B P10-10 stubs and added a fourth (test_baseline_failure_threshold_reporting). Path (b) per scaffold: kept the marker-coverage stub (rescoped by implementer — original PLAN-B premise that all P10 tests carry @nightly didn't match reality, since most Phase 10 tests are @integration; rewritten to assert what is actually load-bearing for the nightly tier).

Minor observation: the four perf-harness tests run in BOTH the default and nightly tiers (project's pyproject.toml addopts excludes slow/gpu/e2e but NOT nightly). Tests are fast (0.18s total) so impact is negligible. Strict tier separation would require adding `not nightly` to addopts — out of P9-2 scope.
Closes P10-10. The full P10-1..P10-10 prerequisite track is complete.
